Title: Daily-Academic: A Semantic Literature Discovery and Journal Tracking Platform for Biomedical Research
Authors: Grigoriadis, D.; Georgakopoulos-Soares, I.; Pavlopoulos, G.; Perdikopanis, N.
Abstract: Objective: Biomedical researchers monitoring newly published literature rely on fragmented combinations of keyword alerts, manual database searches, journal subscriptions and repository portals. We aimed to develop and evaluate an integrated platform that unifies semantic literature discovery, journal monitoring and linked omics dataset exploration within a single researcher-oriented workflow, driven by a user profile that remains explicit and editable. Methods: Daily-Academic aggregates publication metadata from biomedical literature repositories and public omics resources and encodes titles and abstracts as dense semantic representations to support similarity-based retrieval beyond keyword matching. Recommendations are ranked by combining semantic relevance to the user profile with publication recency and journal-level preferences. The profile is derived from three user-supplied signals: a free-text statement of research interests, an optional link to the user's own publication record, and interaction history. Retrieval quality was assessed on an offline benchmark of 30 biomedical queries over a fixed corpus of 259,246 publications, comparing Daily-Academic with a lexical BM25 baseline and a PubMedBERT bi-encoder under pooled assessment with graded relevance judgements. Conclusion: Integrating semantic retrieval into a unified discovery workflow with an inspectable user model improved the quality of top-ranked biomedical literature relative to established lexical and dense baselines. Because the benchmark is user-free, the adaptive component of personalisation was inactive and the ranking weights untuned; the observed advantage therefore reflects the semantic representation rather than adaptive personalisation. The platform is publicly available at https://www.daily-academic.com.
